props.body: Your Astro project stays an Astro project. The editor reads your theme's own schemas, writes predictable JSON to disk, and is gone when you build for production.
props.heading: Techy? Good. There's more.

points.description: Your Zod schemas drive the editor, so it can only write fields your components render. No orphan keys, no raw HTML blobs.

props.heading: Fair questions, straight answers.

items.a: In your repo. One JSON file per page in content/pages/, the site settings in content/site.json, images in src/assets/uploads/. Review it in a pull request like any other change.

No. Your live site is a static build with no editor, no server and no database to poke. The editor runs on your machine in astro dev, or, if you add it, on a separate admin address behind a GitHub sign-in.
items.q: Does the editor ship to my live site?

items.a: Yes. Add the online editor and they sign in with GitHub and edit in the browser. Access follows the repository, so there are no extra accounts to manage.
items.q: Can my client use it without a terminal?

items.a: Yes. Once the site is created, the template is yours: change its components and styles, or add a section type with a schema, defaults and a component. The editor picks it up.
items.q: Can I use my own design?

items.a: Anywhere that serves static files. The host runs npm run build and publishes dist. The optional online editor is the one part that needs a server; it is tested on Vercel.
Nothing. It is MIT licensed, and the site it creates is yours. Keep the $99 a month.
